chunk_text:
Implementing Branding
The POLIVY Global Brand Book is your guide to understanding the POLIVY brand and serves as the visual foundation
for all materials related to POLIVY. Each version provides critical elements related to positioning and branding
POLIVY. In this version, you will find an introduction to our new 1L campaign, core branding for materials benefiting
from a more clinical look and feel, and detailed guidance on print and digital layouts.
What’s in the Brand Book?
• Guidelines for brand positioning, personality, and values
• Brand elements such as the logo, color palette, typography, and key graphics
• 1L DLBCL creative campaign implementation guide
• Layout designs for print and digital
• Video animations
• Core branding guidelines for ancillary audiences and scientific communication
• Guidelines for existing and future R/R campaigns
• Data visualisation guidelines and source files
• Internal excitement materials
Local adaptation
Local POLIVY teams are responsible for ensuring compliance with local regulations. While some elements may
require local customization, adhering to these branding guidelines will ensure that POLIVY is globally unified in
imagery and design, thus maximizing the brand's success.
1L=first line; DLBCL=diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; HCP=healthcare professional;
R/R=relapsed/refractory; SOP=standard operating procedure.
Finding other key resources
When developing materials, be sure to refer to other key assets available on the Roche Branding Library here.

Implementing Branding: 1L and Core Branding
1L DLBCL creative campaign
The POLIVY 1L DLBCL campaign is intended for use in promotional print and digital materials
aimed at healthcare professionals. It features a unique, eye-catching, and patient-centric
depiction of the clinical benefit POLIVY offers to patients.

Core branding
Core branding has been developed for use in materials in which the launch campaign
cannot or should not be used, such as materials requiring a more clinical feel,
educational materials, or materials for ancillary audiences. The core branding leverages
the POLIVY logo in an enlarged blue-tinted droplet icon: the Droplet Supergraphic.
1L=first-line; DLBCL=diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

Implementing Branding: Relapsed/Refractory
1L=first line; BR=bendamustine and rituximab; DLBCL=diffuse large
B-cell lymphoma; R/R=relapsed/refractory.
Scenario 1: Countries with existing R/R campaigns
Once the market is ready to launch POLIVY for 1L DLBCL, retire the R/R campaign and
adopt the new 1L campaign. The overall promotional focus should now be on 1L, and in
instances in which 1L and R/R data may be presented together (websites, congresses,
etc), please only leverage the 1L campaign.
Scenario 2: Countries planning to launch Pola+BR for R/R DLBCL in
advance of the 1L launch
If you are planning to launch POLIVY for R/R DLBCL (in advance of the POLARIX
launch), please leverage core branding elements, to allow for a seamless transition to the
1L campaign upon launch.

1L DLBCL Creative Campaign
POLIVY: “Living Numbers”
The POLIVY “Living Numbers” campaign is designed to depict the impressive clinical benefit seen in the POLARIX trial in a
manner that is clear, joyful, hopeful, intriguing, and patient-centric. This campaign is for use primarily for promotional print
and digital materials targeting healthcare professional audiences.
The image features a bustling, lively “27%,” showcasing the primary endpoint from the POLARIX trial in a manner that
connects the clinical data to potential patient impact. The clinical benefit is featured very prominently, letting the data speak
for itself. The crowded scene conveys a sense of celebration, which is appropriate given that POLARIX is the first
trial in approximately 20 years to clinically meaningfully change the standard of care in 1L DLBCL — a potentially
curative setting.

The overall safety profile of POLIVY-R-CHP is similar to that of R-CHOP and consistent
with the known risk of the individual study drugs. Additionally:
• POLIVY-R-CHP had fewer cases of PN leading to discontinuations (0.2% vs R-CHOP: 0.9%)
• Of patients who experienced any grade PN, a lower percentage had Grade ≥2 or higher events
with POLIVY-R-CHP compared with R-CHOP (POLIVY-R-CHP: 13.8% vs R-CHOP: 16.7%)
• Rates of FN were higher with POLIVY-R-CHP vs R-CHOP (14.3% vs 8.0%), but this did not
translate into greater overall rates of infection: Grade 3 or 4 infections were comparable
(15.2% vs 12.6%, respectively)
Drug deliverability favours POLIVY-R-CHP vs R-CHOP
• There was a lower incidence of AEs leading to any dose reduction in the POLIVY-R-CHP arm
(9.2% vs 13.0% for R-CHOP)
• The adherence to treatment was comparable in both arms, however more patients received all
planned doses of polatuzumab vedotin/vincristine in the POLIVY-R-CHP arm vs R-CHOP (91.7%
vs 88.5%)

Primary typeface
Brother 1816 has been
selected as a clear, precise,
contemporary typeface that also
complements the logotype.
It has an elegant simplicity that
emulates the characteristics of
VABYSMO, bringing a powerful
and refined quality to
communications.
This confidence and strength
stands out in a crowded
marketplace, suggesting gravitas
and directness.
We have four weight options for
headers and body copy in print
and digital assets.

Typography specimen and mockup collage: left panel shows 'PRINT / BROTHER 1816' with large 'AaBbCc123 Brother' sample alphabet on lime green background above a purple/lime triangular VABYSMO ad mockup with model hands and text 'VEGF-A' and 'ANG-2'; right side shows assorted digital mockups including a purple outdoor banner reading 'Up to VEGF-A ANG-2 16-week durability' with the VABYSMO logo, two 'READ MORE' buttons (lime and purple), a blue-purple gradient panel with '04', a beach photo of a woman in a red dress with text 'Extended durability', a purple/yellow radial percentage chart showing '50%' and '75%', and a blue circular icon with the number '2'. (page 51, classification: informational)

Digital font

media, such as in PPT, Google
slides, websites and emails.

Fallback font
While Jost is our designated
digital font, there are some
rare occasions where it may
cause technical challenges. If
and when these are identified,
Open Sans is the chosen
fallback option. Open Sans is a
Google font that has an
aesthetic connection to Jost,
ensuring our materials retain
the same look and feel even in
situations where Jost is not an
option.
